text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT DETECTED: API Gateway 502/504 spike in us-west-2 edge tier. Automated alerting paged SRE oncall. Service impact: sporadic 502/504s, increased latency for some customers. Severity: P2. Link: https://ops.example.com/incidents/1827501111 :rotating_light:

alex.k: acked, oncall here. grabbing logs and envoy admin now.

maria.s: i'm seeing alerts too, dashboards show error rate from 0.3% -> 8% in last 6m. 504s primarily.

alex.k: confirm new deploy 20m ago? any canaries?

tom.s: yes, a small routing change to envoy config rolled ~22m ago for weighted backend routing (release r-2026-03-14). canary passed but rollout continued.

alex.k: rolling that back now to previous config. running: `kubectl -n gateway set image deploy/gateway gateway=image:v2026-03-14-rollback`

eng-ops: heads up, I've queued a manual traffic split to route 30% to standby region while we investigate.

maria.s: query of envoy admin shows backends with 5xx spikes and upstream connection errors: `cluster_outlier_ejections` increasing. posting snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T15:02:11Z] cluster gateway-backend-1: remote_close
[2026-03-14T15:02:12Z] cluster gateway-backend-2: no_healthy_upstream
[2026-03-14T15:02:13Z] response_flags: U,LR
```

alex.k: rollback applied, kube reports rollout done. but still seeing 504s at edge level. possibility: upstream overload/connection pools exhausted.

infra-bot: autoscaling event: gateway-backend ASG scaled +3 instances 10m ago. CPU low on those nodes.

maria.s: suggest temporarily increase upstream connection timeout and enable envoy's `retry_on = reset`? also consider disabling HTTP/2 multiplexing to reduce head-of-line blocking.

alex.k: enabling more conservative timeouts and bumping max_connections for upstream clusters. running envoy config reload now.

lucas.p: @olivia.cs can you draft a customer-facing note in case impacted customers ask? CS wants list of affected orgs.

olivia.cs: on it. pulling list from error logs by org id. will post short note: "We're investigating intermittent 5xx from the API gateway; mitigation in progress."

maria.s: after envoy config change, errors dropped to ~2%, but we still have intermittent spikes ~1-2m windows. looking at TCP reset rates from load-balancer.

alex.k: running `tcpdump` on problematic gateway instance to see reset storm. `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 443 and tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-rst) != 0`

eng-ops: we see SYN retries from a handful of backend pods flagged with high accept queue. kernel backlog full on those nodes. looks like ephemeral port exhaustion on upstream side.

maria.s: okay that's consistent. setting envoy outlier detection to eject hosts faster and draining unhealthy upstreams. also enabling short-circuit cache at gateway for idempotent health-check endpoints to reduce load.

alex.k: I've opened an incident bridge (Zoom) — joining now: zoom.us/j/999999999.

oncall-bot: Handoff: alex.k -> maria.s for next 30 minutes while alex focuses on tracing analysis.

maria.s: documenting mitigation runbook steps here: 1) rollback envoy routing (done) 2) increase upstream connect timeout to 10s 3) adjust max_connections 4) enable outlier ejection for cluster 5) route 30% traffic to standby 6) contact top 10 customers with temporary guidance.

olivia.cs: drafted message and shared with lucas.p for approval.

lucas.p: approved. send via status.redwood.ai and DM top customers. tag customers A123, B456, C789 as high impact.

alex.k: tracing shows majority of 504s correlate with long DNS lookup times from a third-party auth service used by our gateway (auth.example-svc). looks like auth upstream is intermittently timing out and holding connections.

maria.s: start bypass for auth check for trusted customers (temp) to reduce dependency. adding header bypass `X-Bypass-Auth: true` for customer IDs in allowlist.

eng-ops: config applied: allowlist for TTL 15m. monitoring for anomalies.

maria.s: errors falling to baseline ~0.4% now. continued monitoring.

olivia.cs: status update sent to customers: "Mitigations applied; we're seeing significant improvement. Engineers are monitoring and will share postmortem."

oncall-bot: Reminder: create postmortem and assign owners within 24h.

tom.s: assigning to SRE-runbooks for follow-up: root cause likely auth upstream flakiness combined with recent routing change that reduced headroom. mitigation: add circuit-breaker to auth calls, increase health-check frequency, and revert to previous routing heuristics.

maria.s: will keep on rotation for next hour to watch for regressions. alex.k, if you finish tracing, can you take the postmortem writeup?

alex.k: yep. I'll compile timelines, config diffs (`git diff release/r-2026-03-14`), and affected customer list.

eng-ops: scaling metrics baseline restored. observing minor error blips <0.5% in last 20m.

olivia.cs: CS notified and queued proactive outreach for impacted customers.

lucas.p: closing bridge in 15m unless we see recurrence. great job coordinating. :clap:

oncall-bot: Incident transitioned to monitoring. Severity downgraded to P3 at 15:42 UTC. Postmortem due.

maria.s: adding action items in runbook: 1) enable auth circuit-breaker 2) improve canary gating for routing changes 3) add synthetic checks for edge 502/504 patterns 4) CS playbook for rapid customer comms.

alex.k: logging off bridge now. final note: don't merge routing change until we've solved auth flakiness.

olivia.cs: thanks team — prepping follow-up comms and CS brief.

end of thread.
